note: entity_share_websub is the base/shim module of a three-module project. It has no config, no routes, no permissions, no Drush; its only code is SignatureTrait (sha256 X-Hub-Signature helper). Real behaviour lives in submodules entity_share_websub_hub (publisher: /subscribe endpoint, subscription DB table, queued notifications) and entity_share_websub_subscriber (subscriber: Subscribe/Unsubscribe buttons, callback routes, settings form). Medium/hard cases are grounded in the fact that the base module's whole role is to be enabled alongside its submodules, which is inspectable via drush pm:list.

evals.prompt: The Drupal contrib project entity_share_websub adds automatic content updates on top of another module. Which existing module does it extend, and which web protocol does its subscription/notification flow imitate?
evals.expected_output: It extends the Entity Share module (which already pulls content over JSON:API) and adds a push layer inspired by the WebSub / PubSubHubbub protocol, so a subscriber site is notified when subscribed content changes instead of polling.

evals.prompt: The entity_share_websub project ships two functional submodules for the two ends of the sync. Name them and say which one makes a site the publisher and which makes it the subscriber.
evals.expected_output: entity_share_websub_hub turns a site into the publishing hub (exposes /subscribe, tracks subscriptions, pushes notifications); entity_share_websub_subscriber turns a site into the subscriber (Subscribe/Unsubscribe buttons on the Entity Share pull form, callback routes, automatic import). The top-level entity_share_websub is only a shared base both depend on.

evals.prompt: In the entity_share_websub base module, what is the single reusable piece of code it provides, and what HTTP header / hashing does it produce to authenticate hub-to-subscriber calls?
evals.expected_output: It provides SignatureTrait with getSignature($data, $secret), which returns 'sha256=' . hash('sha256', $secret . serialize($data)). Both submodules use it to set and validate the X-Hub-Signature header on every callback.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the entity_share_websub project is installed. Inspect the running site and list which of the two functional submodules provided by the entity_share_websub project (the hub end and the subscriber end) are currently enabled.
evals.expected_output: Both entity_share_websub_hub and entity_share_websub_subscriber are enabled (drush pm:list --status=enabled shows them alongside the entity_share_websub base module).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the entity_share_websub base module is enabled but its publisher submodule is not. Enable the entity_share_websub_hub submodule so this site can act as a WebSub publishing hub.
evals.expected_output: entity_share_websub_hub is installed/enabled (e.g. `drush en entity_share_websub_hub -y`), which also pulls in entity_share_server. drush pm:list shows it as Enabled and its /subscribe route becomes available.
